newsitem.title: INDIA: Unexpected low festival demand hurts Indian sugar.
newsitem.headline: Unexpected low festival demand hurts Indian sugar.

text.p: Unexpectedly low festival demand saw Indian sugar prices slump on Friday, dealers said.
"Lower than expected festival buying as well as increased offerings by stockists and millers dragged down prices," one dealer said.

Ready delivery sugar S-30 fell by 25/31 rupees to 1,260/1,300 rupees per quintal while M-30 lost 15/25 rupees at 1,295/1,360 rupees. Sugar mill delivery fell to 1,200/1,220 rupees against 1,225/1,245 rupees.
"Supplies remained high in the market following higher offerings by mill owners," another broker said.
